objective: Separate retrieval accuracy from serialization validity for the completed Q35 context holdout, because the prompt contains eight numbered requests but does not require JSON and the request has no response_format constraint.

semantic_extraction_order: If the full response parses as a JSON object, compare exact expected keys and exact values.

Otherwise, if the response contains a complete numbered answer list, map its unique lines 1 through 8 to the eight REQUESTS in prompt order. Prefer a clearly labeled Final Answers section; accept a bare 1..8 list because the prompt itself numbers the requests in that same order.

Otherwise, parse only explicit Answer fields inside a section whose case ID matches the expected case ID; do not count source quotations, revoked values, distractor cases, or arbitrary occurrences of expected strings elsewhere in the response.
Count exact value equality only after trimming whitespace and surrounding Markdown emphasis/backticks; do not normalize case, punctuation inside values, units, or identifiers.
method.incomplete_outputs: Keep finish_reason=length as incomplete. Record any unambiguous explicit answers as partial semantic coverage, but do not compare that run as a complete quality result.
method.ambiguity_policy: If a question has multiple conflicting explicit answers or the answer-to-question mapping is ambiguous, mark that item unresolved rather than choosing the answer that matches the fixture.
method.reporting: For each run report original JSON exact-match score, strict JSON validity, semantic exact-match score, extraction path, completion status, and unresolved item numbers. Do not overwrite the original score.

decision_rule: Only completed responses with an unambiguous semantic score can support a context-quality comparison. A high semantic score with invalid JSON means retrieval succeeded while output-format compliance failed. Context adoption still requires the same-fixture comparison across contexts and separate operational cost/speed evidence.
scope_limit: This audit re-scores existing deterministic receipts only. It does not change the holdout, generation, model, context, sampling, request cap, harness, or original benchmark results.
